name: The Cheesy Classic
shortDesc: Our house burger: a smashed beef patty, aged cheddar and burnt-butter onions in a toasted brioche bun.
description: The one the kitchen is named for. We smash the patty thin on a screaming-hot flat top so the edges catch and crisp, then melt aged cheddar over it while it rests. Underneath goes a spoonful of onions cooked down slowly in burnt butter until they turn sweet and jammy; on top, house pickles for the sharpness that cuts through it all. Served in a brioche bun toasted in the same pan the beef came out of.

name: Margherita Italiana
shortDesc: San Marzano tomato, fior di latte and basil on a 48-hour dough, blistered fast in a hot oven.
description: Three ingredients with nowhere to hide, so all three have to be right. The dough proves for 48 hours, which is what gives the cornicione its open, airy structure and a faint sourdough tang. San Marzano tomatoes are crushed by hand, never cooked, so they stay bright. Fior di latte goes on in torn pieces and basil goes on after the bake, so it perfumes the pizza instead of scorching.

name: Roast Chicken Platter
shortDesc: Half a bird brined overnight, roasted until the skin shatters, with pan gravy and warm flatbread.
description: We brine the chicken overnight in salt, bay and black pepper, which seasons it right through and keeps the breast from drying out. It roasts breast-down first, then flips for the last stretch so the skin crackles. Everything that renders into the tray becomes the gravy — nothing thickened, nothing wasted. Comes with flatbread warmed over the flame to mop the plate.

name: Double Smash Burger
shortDesc: Two thin patties, double cheese and house sauce — built for people who found one patty insufficient.
description: The Classic, doubled, and rebalanced so it doesn't collapse into itself. Two thin patties are smashed and stacked with a slice of cheese between them as well as on top, so the cheese binds the layers rather than sliding off the side. House sauce, shredded lettuce and pickles keep it from turning heavy. It is a two-hands burger and we are not going to pretend otherwise.

name: Flame-Grilled Chicken
shortDesc: Marinated thigh meat over open coals, finished with charred lemon and a green herb sauce.
description: Thigh rather than breast, because thigh takes the heat of live coals without seizing up. It marinates in yoghurt, garlic and toasted spice for a day, which tenderises the meat and gives it the dark, blistered crust you get off a real fire. Off the grill it's hit with lemon charred cut-side down on the same coals, and a loose herb sauce — parsley, coriander, green chilli — spooned over.

name: Tomato & Basil Pizza
shortDesc: Slow-roasted tomatoes, garlic confit and torn basil — the lighter one, and the kitchen's own favourite.
description: Tomatoes are halved and roasted low and slow until they collapse and concentrate, then scattered over the base with cloves of garlic confited in olive oil until they're sweet and spreadable. There's less cheese here than on the Margherita by design; this one is about the fruit. Torn basil and a last pour of olive oil go on as it leaves the oven.

name: Creamy Cheese Pasta
shortDesc: Ribbons of pasta in a glossy three-cheese sauce, finished with cracked pepper and lemon zest.
description: The sauce is built in the pan from the pasta water itself, not from cream poured out of a carton — starch and cheese emulsified together until it turns glossy and clings to every ribbon. Three cheeses go in: one for salt, one for melt, one for the funk. Cracked black pepper and a little lemon zest at the end stop it from becoming heavy going by the third forkful.
